page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-24xCPU-256GB is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 24 vCPUs allocated on a shared basis. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz and includes 16 MB of L3 cache. The server is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 10.67 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks reveal a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance under stress-ng is poor, falling into the bottom 10%, which reflects the shared CPU allocation and moderate 2.0 GHz clock speed. However, multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU scores reach average levels. Notably, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is strong, placing in the top 25% of benchmarks. Memory bandwidth remains average for both small and large block reads, though the overall Passmark memory score is weak. Database operations and Redis SET operations perform at average levels.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU model combined with a dense 256.0 GB memory footprint offers a resource-heavy profile without the premium cost of dedicated cores. This makes the server highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained, high-performance single-core execution. Recommended workloads include large-scale caching layers, multi-threaded data decompression, memory-bound database operations, and general-purpose web serving.
